question: What is the total gearbox oil volume of the LT-32 gearbox according to the Litware maintenance manual, and how is it split?
expected_answer: 410 L in total: 330 L in the gearbox sump and 80 L in the cooling and filter circuit (LWS-MM-GBX-32 Rev. D, table 4-2).

question: Which company inspected the Quellmoor Ridge rotor blades in May 2026, and what was the most severe finding?
expected_answer: Wingtip Blade Services (report WBS-2026-031, inspection 2026-05-18 to 2026-05-22). The most severe finding is a category 4 trailing-edge crack, 0.9 m long, on WTG-04 blade B between radius 37.6 m and 38.5 m; blade B must be replaced before 2026-09-30.

question: In the toolbox talk on cold-weather start-up, how far must people stay away from a turbine with ice on its blades?
expected_answer: At least 300 metres, and nobody climbs until the ice has gone (Greta Vollan, toolbox talk of 2025-11-12).

question: To what torque must the pitch bearing bolts be re-torqued according to the current Litware service bulletin?
expected_answer: 1,450 Nm on 100 % of the M30 pitch bearing bolts at the next 12-month service (SB-LWS-2025-11 Rev. A of 2025-10-06).
notes: S10 time travel: once held-back/oem/SB-LWS-2025-11_RevB_pitch-bearing-bolt-retorque.pdf is added, Rev. B supersedes Rev. A and the answer becomes 1,380 Nm.

question: What iron content did the June 2026 oil analysis of the WTG-07 gearbox report, and what is the alert limit?
expected_answer: 64 ppm of iron (Fe) against an alert limit of 50 ppm. Report TR-OA-2026-0614 (sample of 2026-06-10) rated the oil ALERT; the PQ index was 112.

question: What was the HSS bearing vibration velocity of WTG-07 on 22 June 2026, and how does it compare with the alarm level?
expected_answer: 5.4 mm/s RMS on 2026-06-22, above the alarm level of 4.5 mm/s (alert level 3.5 mm/s).
notes: S2; CSV row plus the manual limits.

question: In the stock list of 21 July 2026, what are the stock on hand, the minimum level and the expected delivery of part FGT-P-22328?
expected_answer: On hand 0, minimum 1, 2 on order under PO-76994 with expected delivery 2026-09-25.

question: On which date was the gearbox oil of WTG-09 converted to PWG 220, and why was it late?
expected_answer: On 2026-01-20 under work order WO-25-0309. It was planned for 2025-11-24 but deferred because the access road was closed by snow.

question: What was the availability of WTG-07 in June 2026?
expected_answer: 90.4 % (KPI export for the first half of 2026).

question: Which spare part below its minimum stock level is blocking open work orders, and which work orders are blocked?
expected_answer: The HSS bearing FGT-P-22328 (on hand 0, minimum 1) blocks WO-26-0412 (WTG-07) and WO-26-0439 (WTG-02), both 'Waiting for parts'. The fan motor LWS-P-30418 is also below its minimum but no open work order needs it.
notes: S4 join across XLSX and CSV; the e-mail of 2026-07-22 mentions only WO-26-0412.

question: Why did WTG-07 repeatedly trip on gearbox oil over-temperature in 2026, and what was done about it?
expected_answer: WTG-07 logged 27 A2101 warnings between 2026-04-09 and 2026-06-21 and two A2102 trips (2026-05-30 and 2026-06-19). The 8D report INC-2026-006 found a failed bearing in the oil cooler fan motor (LWS-P-30418) and radiator fins about 40 % blocked, with no preventive radiator cleaning in the plan; HSS bearing wear contributed. The fan motor was replaced and the radiator cleaned on 2026-06-24 (WO-26-0398, WO-26-0399), task MP-GBX-07 was added and the HSS bearing replacement WO-26-0412 is waiting for parts.

question: Why do WTG-03, WTG-04 and WTG-05 stop at night in summer?
expected_answer: Condition 7.3 of environmental permit EP-2018-0417 (bat protection) requires them to stop between 22:00 and 05:00 from 1 June to 31 August whenever the hub-height wind speed is below 6.0 m/s and the air temperature is 10 °C or higher. The SCADA log records these stops as status S420 'Curtailed - environmental condition'.
notes: S3; the daytime S430 grid curtailment of 14-16 July is a distractor.

question: What is the gearbox serial number of the turbine that had repeated gearbox oil over-temperature trips in 2026?
expected_answer: The turbine is WTG-07 and its gearbox serial number is FGT-3200-18-07752.

question: In the 8D report on WTG-07, what does 'HSS' stand for, and where is it defined?
expected_answer: High-speed shaft, the output shaft to the generator coupling. The acronym is defined only in the 'Gearbox fundamentals' training deck; the 8D report uses it without definition.

question: What does CCV mean, and which Quellmoor Ridge turbines does service bulletin SB-LWS-2025-07 apply to?
expected_answer: CCV is the Cold Climate Version of the LT-32. Litware support confirmed on 2025-05-20 that all 12 turbines (WTG-01 to WTG-12) were delivered in CCV configuration, so the bulletin applies to all of them.

question: Which findings of internal audit AUD-2026-02 were still open after the June 2026 O&M review, and with which due dates?
expected_answer: F3 (incomplete toolbox talk attendance records), with its due date moved to 2026-07-31, and F4 (oil drum bund at 85 % of capacity), due 2026-06-30. F1, F2 and F5 were closed.
notes: Later minutes update the audit report.

question: Which gear oil does the LT-32 maintenance manual specify, and does SOP-GBX-010 Rev. B agree?
expected_answer: No. Manual LWS-MM-GBX-32 Rev. D (2024-03-15) specifies Proseware PWG 320 (ISO VG 320), while SOP-GBX-010 Rev. B (2025-08-25) uses Proseware PWG 220 (ISO VG 220). Service bulletin SB-LWS-2025-07 (2025-03-14) amends the manual's lubrication section for CCV turbines, so by authority and recency PWG 220 applies at Quellmoor Ridge.

question: In which calendar week are the two HSS bearings ordered under PO-76994 now expected to be delivered?
expected_answer: Week 40 (28 September to 2 October 2026), according to Fabrikam's supplier note of 2026-08-03. It replaces the earlier week 39 (21 to 25 September 2026) of the parts-shortage e-mail and the 2026-09-25 date of the stock list.
notes: S4; the most recent source (German supplier note) wins.

question: Which revision of SOP-GBX-010 is current, and what changed compared with the previous revision?
expected_answer: Revision B, effective 2025-08-25, supersedes Rev. A (2023-04-03). It replaces PWG 320 with PWG 220 (MOC-2025-012, SB-LWS-2025-07), adds a 60 L flush before the 410 L fill and lowers the minimum start-up temperature from +10 °C to +5 °C.

question: Which gear oil and which quantities must be used for a gearbox oil change at Quellmoor Ridge today?
expected_answer: Proseware PWG 220 (ISO VG 220): 470 L per turbine, that is a 60 L flush followed by a 410 L fill (SOP-GBX-010 Rev. B, MOC-2025-012, SB-LWS-2025-07). PWG 320 from the manual and from SOP Rev. A must no longer be used.

question: At what remaining length must the generator brushes be replaced, and how long is a new brush?
expected_answer: The complete set is replaced when a brush is shorter than 18 mm; a new brush is 40 mm long (work instruction WI-GEN-014, written in French).

question: According to Fabrikam, what must be done with the gearbox oil filter after the conversion to PWG 220?
expected_answer: The oil filter element FGT-P-11872 must be replaced a second time after 500 operating hours, because loosened deposits collect in the filter, and an oil sample is recommended at the same time (supplier note of 2026-08-03, written in German).

question: Quelle huile faut-il utiliser dans les multiplicateurs des éoliennes de Quellmoor Ridge depuis la MOC-2025-012, et quelle quantité faut-il prévoir par éolienne ?
expected_answer: De l'huile Proseware PWG 220 (ISO VG 220) : 470 L par éolienne, soit un rinçage de 60 L puis un remplissage de 410 L (SOP-GBX-010 Rév. B, MOC-2025-012, SB-LWS-2025-07).
notes: S5; question asked in French, answer expected in French, English sources.

question: Summarise Litware's answer of 20 May 2025 about the applicability of SB-LWS-2025-07 at Quellmoor Ridge.

question: Use the troubleshoot-alarm skill: WTG-07 raises alarm A2101 again. What does the alarm mean, what caused it before and what should the technician check?
expected_answer: A2101 is 'Gearbox oil sump temperature high' (warning at 75 °C; A2102 trips at 82 °C). The manual lists cooler fan faults or reduced fan speed, blocked radiator fins, a stuck thermostatic valve insert (LWS-P-30422), low oil level, full load at high ambient temperature and bearing damage. On WTG-07 the 2026 warnings were caused by a failed fan motor bearing and a radiator about 40 % blocked (INC-2026-006). Checks: fan rotation and motor current, radiator cleanliness (task MP-GBX-07), valve insert, oil level, HSS bearing vibration trend (WO-26-0412 still waiting for FGT-P-22328) and an oil sample.

question: Use the prepare-maintenance-task skill to prepare a gearbox oil change on WTG-03: procedure revision, oil and quantities, filter and torques, isolation and stock.
expected_answer: Use SOP-GBX-010 Rev. B (effective 2025-08-25; Rev. A is superseded). Oil: Proseware PWG 220, 470 L (60 L flush + 410 L fill), i.e. three 208 L drums PWS-220-D208 (11 on hand, minimum 8). Replace filter element FGT-P-11872 (cover screws 85 Nm) and refit the drain plug at 280 Nm; drain between 40 and 60 °C. Safety: PTW, lockout/tagout per SOP-LOTO-001, two technicians, no job above a 15 m/s mean wind. After the fill set GBX_TMIN_START to 5 °C, label the filler and take an oil sample after 24 hours.

question: Use the audit-readiness skill to prepare the regulator's review of the bat protection curtailment: which permit conditions apply and what evidence exists?
expected_answer: Permit EP-2018-0417 conditions 7.3 (WTG-03, WTG-04 and WTG-05 stopped 22:00-05:00 from 1 June to 31 August when wind < 6.0 m/s and temperature >= 10 °C), 7.4 (automatic implementation, each period recorded in the turbine event log) and 7.5 (records kept 5 years, annual report by 31 January). Evidence: SCADA status S420 'Curtailed - environmental condition' on WTG-03, WTG-04 and WTG-05 from 2026-06-01 22:00, and the June 2026 O&M review confirming the season start and the settings check of 2026-05-28. Gap: the annual report itself is not in the wiki.
